name: memory-loop-scenario
description: Declarative walk-through data for the living-memory loop, about the `memory-loop-demo` capability defined in 01-baseline.json: a session that produced observations, four staged claims spanning the three states the curation queue handles (linked, unlinked, and a contested pair), one proposal already open for review, one capability request raised against the demo capability's owner, and one auto-promote allowlist entry. This mirrors, as data, the exact sequence tests/integration/test_memory_loop_e2e.py exercises against a live database by calling ClaimService, ConsolidationService, and PromotionService directly -- a human walking the curation-queue and promotion-review surfaces by hand can reproduce it claim by claim from this file. `make dev-seed` executes every section below through those same services (see scripts/seed.py::apply_memory_loop_section) rather than writing their tables directly -- each is owned by exactly one service, the same structural rule a lint gate enforces for production code.

session_events.body: Who owns the memory-loop-demo capability, what's its lifecycle state, and who owns the upcoming mobile checkout redesign?

Observed from the conversation: the platform team owns memory-loop-demo, it is GA, and the mobile checkout redesign (no matching capability in this tenant) is owned by the checkout team. Staged as claims for review.

staged_claims.subject: memory-loop-demo
staged_claims.notes: Subject resolves to a real entity -- the ordinary case the curation queue never has to touch. This is the claim 02-scenario.json's own open proposal (below) is for.

staged_claims.subject: the upcoming mobile checkout redesign

evidence.excerpt: mobile checkout redesign is owned by the checkout team

staged_claims.notes: The subject reference does not resolve to any entity in this tenant, so ClaimService.stage_claim stages it `unlinked` rather than dropping it -- it waits in the curation queue for a curator to link it to the right entity once one exists, or discard it.

staged_claims.subject: memory-loop-demo
staged_claims.notes: First half of the contested pair: same subject and predicate as its counterpart below, from a comparable authority tier, so consolidation records both as contested rather than one superseding the other -- exactly the state REASON_CONTESTED surfaces in the curation queue for a human to resolve.

staged_claims.subject: memory-loop-demo
staged_claims.notes: Second half of the contested pair, disagreeing with its counterpart about the same subject's lifecycle_state.

promotion_proposals.notes: Consolidated (a plain ADD -- nothing else claims memory-loop-demo's ownership yet) and proposed, waiting on a human reviewer. Left open rather than auto-accepted because the default posture is nobody's predicate is auto-promoted until a tenant opts it in -- see autopromote_allowlist below, which opts in a different predicate.

capability_requests.subject: memory-loop-demo
capability_requests.title: Document memory-loop-demo's retry policy
capability_requests.body: Consuming this capability's API and can't find retry/backoff guidance -- could the owning team add it to the capability's facts?

autopromote_allowlist.notes: Runbook links are low-risk to auto-promote, so this predicate (not owned_by_team, which the open proposal above is for) is opted into the sweep's automatic-acceptance path.
